summary: A confirmation the user cannot pass through by reflex, for actions that cannot be undone.
useWhen: the action deletes data, revokes access, cancels a subscription, or otherwise cannot be reversed by the user
the action applies to more than one record at once — bulk destructive actions need this even when a single one would not
structure: A Modal whose title names the action and the object — "Delete 14 projects", not "Are you sure?".
Body text stating what is lost and what is not, in that order.
For high-consequence actions, an Input requiring the object's name to be typed exactly before the confirm Button enables.
Footer: cancel first in the DOM, destructive second — so the safe option is reached first by keyboard.

loading.must: Disable both footer Buttons and say what is happening on the destructive one. Keep the Modal open.
loading.why: closing the modal optimistically leaves the user unsure whether the deletion happened when it later fails

empty.must: Never open with nothing selected. If the selection emptied while the modal was opening, close it.
empty.why: "Delete 0 items" is a dialog with no purpose that still teaches the user to click through confirmations

error.must: Keep the Modal open, show an Alert with `intent="error"` inside it, and leave the confirm Button usable for a retry.
error.why: a failed deletion that closes the dialog reads as a successful one

partial.must: For bulk actions, report how many succeeded and name what did not, with a retry limited to the failures.
partial.why: "some items could not be deleted" with no list means the user must re-check every record by hand

requires: `title` on the Modal — it is the dialog's accessible name
the cancel Button before the destructive one in DOM order
a confirm Button that names the action, not "OK"
notes: Modal already contains focus, closes on Escape and hides the rest of the page. Escape must cancel, never confirm.
Typed confirmation is friction on purpose. Use it where the consequence justifies it and nowhere else, or it becomes something to type without reading.

antiPatterns.why: it names neither the action nor the object, so the answer is a reflex

antiPatterns.dont: the destructive Button focused by default
antiPatterns.why: Enter on an unread dialog then performs the irreversible action

antiPatterns.dont: a Toast as the only confirmation of a destructive action
antiPatterns.why: a toast disappears, and so does the undo it was carrying

antiPatterns.dont: a confirmation dialog on every action
antiPatterns.why: confirmations that appear for reversible actions train the user to dismiss the ones that matter
